speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help narrow this down, have you noticed any hearing loss, tinnitus, or a sensation of fullness in your ear on the affected side? Additionally, do these spells worsen with specific head movements, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the brief duration and positional trigger are very suggestive. To further differentiate between vestibular migraine, Meniere's disease, or a central cause like a stroke, have you experienced any recent severe headache, visual changes, double vision, or difficulty speaking since the episode? Also, do you have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or prior migraines?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
